solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Rhythmic jazz lead accepts honour in retirement

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in, so one piece goes inside the other
retiring means going back, so the combined letters are read from the end to the start

blocks.note: Pb is the chemical symbol for lead
the Order of the British Empire, a British honour

explanation.surface: A jazz bandleader with a steady beat takes a royal honour once he has retired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' looks like a bandleader, but it is the metal; P(OBE)B read backwards gives BEBOP.
explanation.definitionFit: Bebop is a fast, rhythmically complex style of jazz that grew up in the 1940s.

clue.text: British brothers who sang about high rise suburb

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for British
the Everly Brothers were an American singing duo
hills are ground that rises high

explanation.surface: British siblings performed a song about a tower block in the suburbs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High rise' suggests a tower block, but here it is rising land.
explanation.definitionFit: Beverly Hills is a wealthy city enclosed within Los Angeles, commonly thought of as a suburb.

clue.text: Boring name, boring idol

indicators.note: something boring drills its way into the middle of something else

blocks.note: Baal was a false god of the Old Testament, worshipped as an idol
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A dull name for a dull pop star.
explanation.walkthrough: The same word does two jobs: the first 'Boring' means dull, the second means drilling into.
explanation.definitionFit: Something banal is so ordinary and predictable that it is tedious.

clue.text: Move stealthily around rogue US spy base

indicators.note: a rogue spy has gone off the rails, so his letters stray from their order

blocks.note: these five letters rearranged
the foot is the base of something

explanation.surface: An American agent gone bad creeps round a military base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Around' belongs to the definition, as in the phrase used of someone avoiding commitment.
explanation.definitionFit: To pussyfoot around is to tread warily like a cat, avoiding any direct move.

clue.text: Secured folio placed in prepared prepaid envelope

indicators.note: something placed in another thing ends up inside it

blocks.note: something prepared has been made
F is the abbreviation for folio
a stamped addressed envelope, sent prepaid for a reply

explanation.surface: A document page is posted securely in a ready stamped envelope.
explanation.walkthrough: SAE is the British abbreviation for a stamped addressed envelope; F goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To have made something safe is to have secured it against danger or loss.

clue.text: "Thousand Island" first class cocktail

blocks.note: Roman numeral for a thousand
an ait is a small island in a river
A1 means first class, with the 1 read as I

explanation.surface: A cocktail built on Thousand Island dressing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thousand Island' looks like the salad dressing; it splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A mai tai is a rum cocktail with lime and orange flavours, linked with Tiki bars.

clue.text: Bank on introduction of Ezra Pound verse

indicators.note: an introduction comes at the start, so only the first letter is wanted

blocks.note: Dogger Bank is a large sandbank in the North Sea
the opening letter of this name
L is the abbreviation for a pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Someone relies on the poet Ezra Pound for an introduction to his verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ezra Pound' reads as the poet, but the name splits: one letter from Ezra, then the money.
explanation.definitionFit: Doggerel is clumsy, badly written comic verse.

clue.text: Driver found stuck in middle of dam

indicators.note: only what is stuck in the middle is wanted, so both ends are cut off

blocks.note: a dam creates a reservoir, and the word is used for a dammed lake

explanation.surface: A motorist is found trapped halfway across a dam.
explanation.walkthrough: Strip two letters from each end of RESERVOIR.
explanation.definitionFit: A servo is a mechanism that drives a larger system, such as a servomotor powering a control.

clue.text: Florida shed housing black echo of the past

indicators.note: a building housing something holds it inside

blocks.note: Fla is an abbreviation for Florida
a shack is a crude hut or shed
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A shed in Florida that once housed slaves recalls a darker history.
explanation.definitionFit: A flashback is a sudden vivid memory or a scene returning to earlier events.

clue.text: Having run out of nail polish, ordered Germanic cosmetic

indicators.note: r is the cricket abbreviation for run, so the run is taken out of the word that follows
putting letters in order means arranging them afresh

blocks.note: nail varnish is nail polish
these eight letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone out of nail polish turns to a German-made beauty product.
explanation.walkthrough: VARNISH loses its R (run) to give VANISH, and GERMANIC is rearranged to finish the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Vanishing cream is a light face cream that seems to disappear into the skin, a cosmetic.

clue.text: Food business needs elastic supply

indicators.note: read as supple-ly, meaning in a pliant way, so the letters bend into new shapes

blocks.note: these twelve letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A food firm requires a supply of elastic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supply' looks like a noun but is the adverb of supple.
explanation.definitionFit: A delicatessen is a shop selling prepared foods such as cold meats and cheeses.

clue.text: Knocking back Castle Cary ale really restricts legs of runners

indicators.note: the phrase restricts the answer, holding it within its own letters
knocking back a drink tips it backwards, so read the letters right to left

blocks.note: the letters run across the words of this phrase

explanation.surface: Drinking real ale in a Somerset town keeps the drinker's legs from running.
explanation.walkthrough: Castle Cary is a small town in Somerset. The answer sits inside 'castlE CARY ALE Really', read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A relay race is run in stages, each leg by a different member of the team.

clue.text: Mineral deposit right in missile launch area?

indicators.note: one letter is set inside the other word

blocks.note: the oche is the line a darts player throws from
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A query about whether some mineral ore lies within a rocket launch site.
explanation.walkthrough: The missile is a dart, and the oche is the throwing line in darts; the question mark flags the playful description.
explanation.definitionFit: Ochre is an earthy clay coloured by iron oxide, dug from natural deposits as a pigment.

clue.text: Hector sent back to carry a plant

indicators.note: carrying something means holding it within
sending something back returns it the way it came, so read it right to left

blocks.note: to hector someone is to harass or worry them
taken as written

explanation.surface: Hector, the Trojan hero, is sent home bearing a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hector' with a capital looks like the Trojan prince but is the verb meaning to bully.
explanation.definitionFit: Yarrow is a common wild flowering herb with feathery leaves, also called milfoil.

clue.text: Shakes round top, not being this?

blocks.note: to rock is to shake
O is round in shape
a lid is a top

explanation.surface: A puzzle about what shaking round the top implies about a thing.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the wordplay: something that shakes is the opposite of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Rock-solid means completely firm and steady, unlike anything that shakes.

clue.text: One year, following winless season, American kid fails to finish course in Japan

indicators.note: without a win, so the word win is removed from the season's name
not finishing means the final letter is dropped
what follows comes after, so the opening pieces are placed behind the season

blocks.note: winter is a season
Roman numeral one
Y is the abbreviation for year
A is the abbreviation for American
taken as written

explanation.surface: After a season without a win, a young American drops out of his Japanese course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Course' suggests study, but here it is a course of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Teriyaki is a Japanese dish of meat or fish glazed with a sweet soy marinade, served as a course.

clue.text: Giant animal droppings make nitrogen beneath one

indicators.note: in a down answer, what lies beneath comes lower, so the pieces before this word go after the numeral

blocks.note: Roman numeral one
guano is bird or bat droppings
to do is to make
N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen

explanation.surface: A huge beast's droppings produce nitrogen fertiliser.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'beneath one' puts the rest below I.
explanation.definitionFit: The iguanodon was a large plant-eating dinosaur of the Cretaceous period.

clue.text: Indiana bangs violate the law

blocks.note: IN is the postal abbreviation for Indiana
bangs is the American word for a fringe of hair

explanation.surface: Loud bangs in Indiana break the law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bangs' suggests explosions, but it is the hairstyle Americans call bangs.
explanation.definitionFit: To infringe is to break or encroach upon a rule or right.

clue.text: Provocative glimpse of the pub, by the sound of it!

indicators.note: this asks the solver to go by what is heard, not what is written

blocks.note: a sighting of an inn, or pub

explanation.surface: Catching sight of the pub is enough to stir someone up.
explanation.definitionFit: Inciting means stirring up or urging on, which is what something provocative does.

clue.text: Hindu returning a Hong Kong carpet

indicators.note: returning means coming back, so the letters are read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: taken as written
HK is the abbreviation for Hong Kong
a rug is a small carpet

explanation.surface: A Hindu brings home a carpet from Hong Kong.
explanation.definitionFit: Gurkhas are Nepalese soldiers, most of them Hindu by religion, so the definition is an example.

clue.text: Clergyman, not very upper-class, succeeded as a high-flyer

indicators.note: not means without, so v, the usual short form of very, is taken away

blocks.note: a vicar is a clergyman
U means upper-class
S is the abbreviation for succeeded

explanation.surface: A modest, not especially posh priest has done well and risen high.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Icarus flew too near the sun on wax wings, the original high flier.

clue.text: Musician Franz at last cuts record

indicators.note: only the very end of the name is wanted
a letter that cuts into a word slices it apart and sits inside

blocks.note: a list is a record of items
the final letter of this name

explanation.surface: Composer Franz finally makes a recording.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Musician Franz' reads as one name, but Franz only supplies its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Liszt was the Hungarian composer and virtuoso pianist of the Romantic era.

clue.text: State vote breaking the laws regularly

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals, here every other one
breaking into something puts one piece in the middle of another

blocks.note: the odd letters of these words
a cross marks a vote on a ballot

explanation.surface: A state's vote regularly breaks the law.
explanation.definitionFit: Texas is the large US state in the south-west.

clue.text: Barring outsiders, try second event: get to assemble again

indicators.note: the outside letters of each word are barred, leaving only their insides

blocks.note: the inside of this word
the inside of this word
the inside of this word
the inside of this word

explanation.surface: Organisers try a second event, wanting outsiders kept out of the gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: Every one of the four words loses its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To reconvene is to meet or gather together again after a break.

clue.text: Madame features in film The Cornwall Tourist?

indicators.note: something that features in a film appears within it

blocks.note: E.T. is the Spielberg film
Mme is the abbreviation for Madame

explanation.surface: A French lady stars in a film called The Cornwall Tourist.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags dialect: Cornish people call tourists emmets, the old word for ants.
explanation.definitionFit: Emmet is the Cornish slang term for a visitor or holidaymaker, originally meaning an ant.

clue.text: Talented Frenchman designing a de luxe mansard

indicators.note: designing something means laying out its parts in a new plan

blocks.note: these fourteen letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A gifted French architect designs a luxury mansard roof.
explanation.walkthrough: A mansard is a roof style named after a French architect, which makes the surface feel architectural.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexandre Dumas was the prolific French novelist behind The Three Musketeers.

clue.text: Penelope's husband liberally used soy sauce at first

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word is wanted
used liberally, the letters are scattered freely rather than kept in order

blocks.note: taken as written
the opening letter of this word

explanation.surface: A wife's husband splashes soy sauce over his food.
explanation.definitionFit: In Homer's Odyssey, Penelope waits faithfully for her husband, the wandering Ithacan king.

clue.text: Intolerable midday temperature inside

indicators.note: the letter is placed inside the other word

blocks.note: noon is midday
T is the abbreviation for temperature

explanation.surface: The midday heat indoors is unbearable.
explanation.definitionFit: Not on is a British idiom for unacceptable, describing behaviour that cannot be tolerated.
